Something I realize more and more, with trading but also with life, is that not everything is under our control, and that more is not necessarily better.

For example, I've been bullish since January/February, when price reached the expected main support zone of $60k-70k:

[https://t.me/CryptoCapoTG_Official/1004], [https://x.com/CryptoCapo_/status/2019434869001195948?s=20]

Since then, 5 months have passed by, which is a lot of time. And price went up to 82k, then back down to 58k, and now trading at around 63k.

During all this time, of course I've reviewed my analysis to see if something was wrong and if price could go lower from here. But, the more I checked, the more it confirmed the bullish bias.

So... to what extent is it healthy to keep checking, to try to control every variable?

In the end, the result is not up to us. Market analysis doesn't give you 100% probabilities, never. There are no guarantees. You can position yourself on the side of probability, and that's what matters. But even more important is knowing how to wait, to have patience. 

And overanalyzing, besides causing unnecessary stress, can make you change your mind simply because what you expect is not happening yet.

The market could remain within a range for more weeks, or it could start going up from here. That's difficult to know. What you need to know is how to not let that affect you while you keep living your life, and how to adapt if something unexpected occurs.

Therefore, the lesson here is trust, acceptance, and detachment. Trust because you've done your best. Acceptance to embrace the reality of the present moment and its timing. And detachment by understanding that the final outcome doesn't fully depend on you. That depends on something much bigger than us.

And this applies to everything in life.

What does “gas” mean in crypto? 

“Gas” is important in the world of crypto. Simply put, gas is the payment needed when making a transaction or interacting with a smart contract on a blockchain — i.e., the network fee you pay. 

Gas is usually paid in the given blockchain’s native cryptocurrency — e.g., ETH is used for transactions on Ethereum, and BNB is used for the same on BNB Smart Chain). These fees go to miners or validators responsible for keeping networks secure and confirming transactions. Gas fees also prevent spam on the network, keeping the blockchain running smoothly.

The seventh round of Israel-Lebanon talks in Rome ended as these negotiations usually do: everyone reported progress, and nothing moved.

Beirut wanted to expand the pilot-zone model to Bint Jbeil or Khiam. Israel said no. The real dispute was not over maps but trust: who verifies that the Lebanese Army has cleared Hezbollah’s armed presence from an area? Israel wants a mechanism it can trust.

📣 EU to revise MiCA rules in 2027 amid US stablecoin push 

⚠️ European Union officials are preparing to revise the bloc’s MiCA crypto framework in 2027 as foreign stablecoin restrictions and faster U.S. rulemaking expose gaps in the existing regime. The planned revision would examine how MiCA treats stablecoins issued outside the European Union. Current requirements have prevented several foreign issuers from receiving authorization, limiting their access to regulated exchanges across the bloc.

💬 “Reopening the file seems unavoidable at this stage,” an unidentified European diplomat told Euronews.

🔗 The diplomat cited positions taken by European institutions, including the European Central Bank, along with changes in global regulation and digital-asset technology. No final proposal has been published. Any amendment would need to pass through the EU’s legislative process before taking effect. The consultation covers developments that have occurred since MiCA entered into application. Its deadline has been extended to Sept. 30, with crypto issuers, service providers, regulators, central banks and finance ministries invited to respond.

"They told me he was gone. They handed me a folded flag and a death certificate. I buried an empty casket in Arlington. For three years, I was a widow. And then my phone rang."

⟁

My husband was a Tier 1 operator. In 2021, his unit was hit during a classified operation in Syria. The official report said he died instantly from an IED. The military liaison came to my house, gave me the speech, and handed me the flag. Because of the "nature of the blast," there was no viewing. Just a closed casket.

I mourned him. I moved on. Or I tried to.

In April 2024, I got a call from an unknown number. The voice on the other end didn't say hello. He just said: "Sarah. It's me. I'm coming home."

I dropped the phone. It was his voice. 

⟁

Two days later, a black SUV pulled up to my house. A man got out. It was my husband. But it wasn't the man I remembered. 

When he "died" in 2021, he was 44 years old. He had scars from two previous deployments. He had a slight limp from a shattered femur in 2014. He looked tired.

The man standing in my driveway looked 30. He had no scars. No limp. He looked exactly the way he did the day we got married.

We sat in the kitchen for six hours while he told me the truth.

⟁

He didn't die in Syria. He was catastrophically injured. 80% burns. Both legs gone. Spinal cord severed. Under normal medical protocols, he would have been dead within minutes. 

But his unit wasn't normal. They medevaced him to a black site in Germany, stabilized him, and transferred him to a subterranean facility in Colorado. 

"They put me in a tank," he told me. "It looked like glass, but it wasn't. They filled it with some kind of gel, and then the lights started. Blue and gold frequencies. I was in and out of consciousness for months."

They didn't just heal his burns. They regenerated his legs. They rebuilt his spine. The technology didn't just fix the damage — it reverted his entire cellular structure back to its peak biological age.

"They kept me there for three years," he said. "Because if I walked out, people would ask questions. You can't explain how a man regrows his legs."

⟁

He was released because of the declassification orders. The military knows they can't hide the facilities much longer. They are quietly sending the "dead" ones home before the truth blows up in their faces.

I am writing this because there are thousands of families who were handed folded flags and empty caskets. Your husbands, your sons, your daughters — some of them aren't dead. They are in the pods. 

The technology exists. It is miraculous. But the fact that they kept it from us — the fact that they let us grieve while they played God in underground bunkers — is unforgivable.
